evidence.claim: Articles 83 and 84 assign the president executive authority, including appointing ministers, directing the federal administration, initiating legislation, promulgating laws, issuing decrees, and vetoing bills, while limiting foreign travel without congressional authorization.
evidence.title: Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil de 1988
evidence.excerpt: Articles 83 and 84 assign the president executive authority, including appointing ministers, directing the federal administration, initiating legislation, promulgating laws, issuing decrees, and vetoing bills, while limiting foreign travel without congressional authorization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary constitutional text in force during 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Defines Bolsonaro's formal authority and constraints in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Formal powers do not prove how they were used in practice.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Bolsonaro had consistently used anti-human-rights discourse, intensified it in government, and questioned the legitimacy of the STF and TSE during the 2022 election campaign.
evidence.title: Respect for human rights must be central during the elections in Brazil
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Bolsonaro had consistently used anti-human-rights discourse, intensified it in government, and questioned the legitimacy of the STF and TSE during the 2022 election campaign.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous NGO commentary focused on the 2022 election context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro's campaign discourse and governing style.
contrary_evidence: It is advocacy-oriented and does not quantify violence by itself.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that Bolsonaro harassed and insulted Supreme Court justices and journalists, tried to undermine trust in the electoral system with unproven fraud claims, and that political violence rose during the campaign season.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Brazil
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that Bolsonaro harassed and insulted Supreme Court justices and journalists, tried to undermine trust in the electoral system with unproven fraud claims, and that political violence rose during the campaign season.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights-monitoring report summarizing 2022 events and their effects.
evidence.period_fit: Events of 2022 summarized in a 2023 country chapter.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's campaign and presidential conduct.
contrary_evidence: The report is broad and includes both Bolsonaro-era climate and later institutional responses.

evidence.claim: HRW reported that the Bolsonaro administration reduced the federal budget to fight violence against women by 90 percent in 2022 compared with 2020.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Brazil
evidence.excerpt: HRW reported that the Bolsonaro administration reduced the federal budget to fight violence against women by 90 percent in 2022 compared with 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Explicit budget figure in a major rights report.
contrary_evidence: Budget cuts do not by themselves prove intent to increase violence, though they weaken protection capacity.

evidence.claim: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and even physical attacks on reporters across Brazil.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro é condenado por dano moral coletivo a jornalistas
evidence.excerpt: A São Paulo court ordered Bolsonaro to pay collective damages to journalists, citing his attacks and threats against the profession and saying they encouraged virtual and even physical attacks on reporters across Brazil.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted judicial finding
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a court ruling with a direct judicial quote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro's conduct toward journalists.
contrary_evidence: The ruling concerns speech and intimidation, not direct state violence.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro called diplomats to repeat false attacks on Brazil's electronic voting system and told them the system was unauditable, prompting a public rebuttal from the TSE.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro chama embaixadores para atacar processo eleitoral; TSE rebate
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro called diplomats to repeat false attacks on Brazil's electronic voting system and told them the system was unauditable, prompting a public rebuttal from the TSE.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with direct attribution and official rebuttal.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the meeting and statements.
contrary_evidence: The conduct is institutional incitement rather than physical violence on its own.

evidence.claim: HRW said the Bolsonaro administration undermined the agency protecting Indigenous peoples, halted recognition of traditional lands, weakened environmental agencies, and left Indigenous territories more vulnerable to encroachment.
evidence.title: Brazil: Indigenous Rights Under Serious Threat
evidence.excerpt: HRW said the Bolsonaro administration undermined the agency protecting Indigenous peoples, halted recognition of traditional lands, weakened environmental agencies, and left Indigenous territories more vulnerable to encroachment.
evidence.source_locator: opening section through paragraph on FUNAI and land recognition
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights-monitoring report focused on Bolsonaro-era policy choices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's administration and appointed officials.
contrary_evidence: Much of the resulting violence was carried out by miners, loggers, and land grabbers rather than by the federal government itself.

evidence.claim: A Reuters report said illegal gold mining on the Yanomami reservation brought disease, violence, and grave human-rights violations, and that the Bolsonaro government showed tacit support for more mining on Indigenous land.
evidence.title: Brazil's largest indigenous reservation overrun by illegal gold mining, says report
evidence.excerpt: A Reuters report said illegal gold mining on the Yanomami reservation brought disease, violence, and grave human-rights violations, and that the Bolsonaro government showed tacit support for more mining on Indigenous land.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting based on a rights report and official policy context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Bolsonaro-era policy environment and stated support for mining on Indigenous land.
contrary_evidence: The immediate abuses were committed by illegal miners, not by the federal government directly.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro used dozens of executive orders to weaken firearms restrictions and aggressively sought to boost gun ownership, prompting resistance from his own federal police.
evidence.title: Exclusive-Brazil federal police warned against Bolsonaro arms agenda, documents show
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Bolsonaro used dozens of executive orders to weaken firearms restrictions and aggressively sought to boost gun ownership, prompting resistance from his own federal police.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting based on official documents and contemporaneous policy context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the arms-liberalization agenda.
contrary_evidence: Supporters framed the policy as lawful self-defense and crime deterrence.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the number of Brazilians registered to own guns surged six-fold after Bolsonaro began loosening gun laws, and that stolen legally registered weapons ended up with violent criminal gangs.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro's gun laws arm Brazil's brazen bank thieves
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the number of Brazilians registered to own guns surged six-fold after Bolsonaro began loosening gun laws, and that stolen legally registered weapons ended up with violent criminal gangs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting linking policy loosening to downstream criminal access.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro policy agenda on guns; downstream criminal use is indirect.
contrary_evidence: The article shows one pathway from liberalization to harm, not a full causal accounting for all gun crime.

evidence.claim: After his defeat, Bolsonaro told supporters to unblock roads, saying protests were part of democracy but road blockades violated people's right to come and go.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro pede que apoiadores liberem estradas e diz que outros protestos são do 'jogo democrático'
evidence.excerpt: After his defeat, Bolsonaro told supporters to unblock roads, saying protests were part of democracy but road blockades violated people's right to come and go.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with direct attributed remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the public appeal and framing of protests.
contrary_evidence: He condemned only the roadblocks, while also legitimizing the surrounding protest movement.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro's challenge to the election result was seen by analysts as weak on the merits but capable of firing up supporters who were already protesting his loss.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro challenge to Brazil election result seen stoking protests
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro's challenge to the election result was seen by analysts as weak on the merits but capable of firing up supporters who were already protesting his loss.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on the immediate political effect of the legal challenge.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro's post-election conduct and its effects.
contrary_evidence: The article discusses potential political impact, not a direct order to protest or violence.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he had sought 'alternatives' after his election defeat but did not detail them, while Reuters reported that he had continued to question the electoral result and claimed to stay within 'the four lines of the Constitution'.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que buscou sem sucesso 'alternativas' após derrota e que não é hora de 'tudo ou nada'
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he had sought 'alternatives' after his election defeat but did not detail them, while Reuters reported that he had continued to question the electoral result and claimed to stay within 'the four lines of the Constitution'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on Bolsonaro's own post-defeat explanation.
contrary_evidence: The statement is ambiguous and does not prove a specific illegal plan.
